token_domain_law: The near-miss tier confirms distance in two declared token domains: y8 (the normalized statement tokens the tier has always used) and renamed (the same statements re-tokenized through the renamed_structure ordinal canonicalization). Both domains share one deletion index construction, one K=1 budget and one canonical witness law. A pair confirmable in both domains is reported exactly once, in the y8 domain: y8 is the token space closest to source and predates the sub-mode, so every fact the tier reported before the sub-mode existed stays byte-identical. Distance zero in the renamed domain is the renamed_structure tier's business and never enters near_miss.

cases.rationale: The empirical corpus PAIR-T3-01 shape: consistent local renames plus consistent receiver-attribute renames plus ONE true inserted clamp. Under y8 tokens the attribute renames price one statement as a replace, so the distance is 2 and the pair is out of budget by rule; under renamed-canonical tokens the renamed statements are equal and the insertion is the only edit.
Local renames only, plus one true inserted clamp: y8 tokens already absorb local renames, so both domains confirm distance 1. The dedup law reports the pair exactly once, in the y8 domain.

Consistent attribute renames plus TWO true inserted statements: renamed-canonical distance is 2, so the pair is out of budget in the renamed domain exactly as a two-edit pair always was in y8. The budget is the declared predicate, not a fixture key.
A pure consistent renaming with no true edit: renamed-canonical distance is 0, which is the renamed_structure tier's business. The near-miss channel must not poach it in either domain.
